title: Recent nearby activity gave no clear added earthquake size estimate gain in global M5.5+ events in 2013-2025
abstract: We tested whether an earlier nearby earthquake improves the chance estimate that a cataloged M5.5+ event reaches M6.0. We used a fixed USGS ComCat snapshot. Ridge logistic models used location-depth groups, with or without a flag for an earlier M5.5+ event within 200 km and seven days. Fits used 6,825 events in 2000-2012. Tests used 5,971 events in 2013-2025. Added activity reduced mean log loss by 0.076%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -0.025% to +0.187%. Thus the primary test gave no clear gain. Some distance and time checks had small positive gains. Excluding the first day reduced gain to 0.018%, with an interval that included zero. For moment-family target magnitudes, the added flag raised log loss by 0.031%. These checks show that the small point gain is sensitive to sample and model choices. The test conditions on occurrence and known location and depth. It does not forecast event times or establish a physical size memory. Catalog error, mixed magnitudes, coarse location controls and 13 test years limit inference. Code, aggregate scores, a figure, source hashes and an independent feature and score audit are supplied.

display.caption: Added activity score gains in the fixed 2013-2025 test. Intervals condition on fitted models and use three-year blocks. All planned settings are shown.

citations.reason: Prior location-controlled size benchmark motivated the added activity question. Same source snapshot; no code reused.
